records.title: From forecast to alert: an open-data AI flood early warning system with reservoir monitoring for the White Volta Basin
records.role: Strong keeper: open-data FEWS and critical evaluation
records.assessment: Read critically: no one-day benefit over persistence; full-feature linear regression is competitive and marginally stronger at high flow at 3/5 days. The independent 2004–2007 test contains no Orange/Red observations; extreme-category results rely on leave-one-year-out evaluation. The GloFAS comparator is reanalysis, not as-issued forecasts. Version provenance is internally unclear (direct v4 versus indirect older-v2.1 wording). Monthly reservoir proxies and retrospective availability do not establish operational input availability. A dissemination architecture does not demonstrate routine deployment. No validation of our models or general local-over-global superiority follows.

records.title: Role of hydrometeorological variables and catchment area to flood generation over the monsoonal climate region of India
records.role: Background: rainfall heterogeneity and antecedent conditions
records.assessment: Useful hydrological interpretation of spatial rainfall, antecedent state and catchment scale. Godavari/VIC monsoonal results, including longer accumulation windows, do not establish transferable Limburg timescales or causal effects. No additional analysis or variables are required by retaining this paper.

records.title: Network-based subbasin-scale mapping of streamflow alteration in Ontario, Canada
records.assessment: Network-based potential regulation is distinct from measured alteration magnitude and timing. It does not prove agency labels incorrect, establish low-head-weir effects, validate structure detection or estimate economic damage.
